newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo rubber prices rise on reduced supply.
newsitem.headline: Colombo rubber prices rise on reduced supply.

text.p: Rubber prices rose at the Colombo auction as buyers scrambled for a rain-reduced 180 tonnes of crepe and 11 tonnes of sheet that were on offer, exporters said.

"A lot of short covering was evident today," a leading exporter said. "Buyers feel they have waited long enough for larger quantities to come into the market. Today they rushed to purchase whatever was available."
Prolonged rain since last month has reduced Sri Lanka's rubber output to very low levels, traders said.
Rain brings production to a virtual standstill and affects the quality of whatever can be tapped.
The average offer at the auction is 200-300 tonnes.
Of the 180 tonnes on offer on Thursday, only 30 tonnes were of the superior grade one-x, brokers said.
Best latex one-x was up one rupee from Tuesday, when the auction was last held, at 76.50.
Number one rose to 74.75 rupees from 73.75 on Tuesday.
